attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post, stated as his view and resting partly on The Information's estimates.

semantics.note: Firm present-tense observation. The context supports reading the COGS as OpenAI's. The proposition drops 'based on the Information's estimates', which is a minor omission and does not change the commitment.

contract.note: No period was named, so using the latest completed quarter and separating COGS from training and R&D costs is a reasonable, ordinary reading. The result depends on the evaluator's choice of period and on where the COGS boundary is drawn.

evidence.note: Contemporaneous secondary summary of a projected full-year loss of up to $5B. It mixes training and inference and is not realized Q2 2024 COGS, so it is context only.
Later annual estimate that implies a roughly 50% inference margin, which cuts against the COGS component. It is an annual estimate built on projections, not realized Q2 2024 data.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no realized Q2 2024 revenue or COGS for OpenAI and no representative results for other providers. e4 shows large projected losses overall. e5 suggests a positive inference margin. Neither meets the contract's measurement requirements, so the claim is unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his post. The Amodei quote that follows is separate and is not part of the claim.

semantics.note: The antecedent (legally acquiring enough data) and his doubt about whether that is possible are both preserved. The consequent, rising training costs, is stated firmly.

contract.note: Requiring the antecedent to be established before scoring follows the speaker's own conditional. Reading 'increasing costs' as total cost per successive frontier training effort is an ordinary reading.

evidence.note: Epoch's 2024 compute-spending breakdown. It does not establish lawful acquisition of the required data or give a comparison of costs across successive models.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional forecast with no deadline. Whether the antecedent occurred is unknown: no evidence shows the required data being acquired lawfully. Under policy an unmet or unknown antecedent is not scored, so the claim stays unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post.

semantics.note: 'I do not believe' is a plain assertion of belief, not graded low or medium confidence. The link to OpenAI's survival is kept. Dropping the belief framing is a minor change.

contract.note: Reading the claim as broad, reliable, economic workflow automation is an ordinary reading. The July 2024 window was the evaluator's choice and is narrow, and the survival threshold is undefined, so interpretation drives the result.

evidence.note: Klarna's own February 2024 disclosure about one customer-service workflow, from before the target period. It is material counterevidence but does not show broad automation.
April 2024 benchmark showing weak general computer-use agents (12% best success). It predates the target period and does not cover all commercial workflows.

reviews.rationale: Both items predate the July 2024 target period and point in opposite directions: one company deployment against one benchmark showing weak agents. Neither establishes the breadth of automation the survival argument requires, so the claim is unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post.

semantics.note: 'Inevitable' and 'will' make this a firm forecast with no deadline. The causal basis (inflated expectations) and both groups, investors and customers, are preserved.

contract.note: Requiring substantial disappointment in both groups, tied to inflated capability expectations, matches the speaker's words. The thresholds are interpretive.

evidence.note: Shows customer backlash after GPT-5, which partly supports the customer component. Much of it stemmed from model removal and broken workflows rather than inflated capability expectations.
A CTO's commentary framing the GPT-5 rollout as a 'failure of expectations' about continuity. It says nothing on investors or the marketing link.
SoftBank, an investor, completing its funding and stating confidence, as its own disclosure. It cuts against investor disappointment but is one investor.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was given, and the early-resolution rule is not met. There is evidence of customer backlash, but investor disappointment linked to inflated expectations is not shown, and SoftBank's continued investment cuts against it. The claim remains unresolved.
